text: Why is ℤ/6ℤ not a field?
choices: 6 is prime, so the field construction fails
explanation: ℤ/nℤ is a field exactly when n is prime; for composite n = 6 = 2·3 the nonzero classes [2] and [3] satisfy [2]·[3] = [0], so they are zero divisors and ℤ/6ℤ is not even an integral domain. It is commutative, does have identity [1], and 6 is composite (not prime), so the other options are false.
